_purpose: Single source of truth for which FRED series are tracked and how they are presented. Both data/update_economic_data.py and js/economy.js read this file, so a series is added or relabelled in ONE place. Do not hardcode series IDs, labels, or units in the Python or JavaScript.

_notes.source_agency: FRED HOSTS series produced by other agencies. The pipeline records each series' real originating agency from the FRED metadata endpoint into fred_data.json as source_agency, and the UI must display that rather than crediting the Federal Reserve for everything.
_notes.chart_default: Series marked chart_default:true are the ones drawn when a category tab is first opened. Others are available via the show/hide legend.
_notes.invert_direction: For series where a RISE is economically unfavourable (unemployment, initial claims, mortgage rate), set invert_direction:true so the UI colours the change indicator correctly. This never changes the value, only how direction is presented.

categories.label: Rates & Credit
categories.description: Policy rate, Treasury yields, the yield curve, mortgage costs, and commercial credit growth. These set the cost of financing data center construction.

categories.label: Inflation & Growth
categories.description: Price indices and aggregate output. Construction and equipment costs track these.

categories.label: Labor & Demand
categories.description: Employment, claims, and retail demand. Labor availability constrains large construction projects.

categories.label: Housing & Construction
categories.description: Housing starts and permits — a leading indicator of regional construction capacity and workforce in-migration.

series.label: Effective Federal Funds Rate
series.tooltip: The interest rate at which banks lend reserves to each other overnight. The Federal Reserve's primary policy rate — it anchors the cost of nearly all other borrowing, including data center project finance.

series.label: 2-Year Treasury Constant Maturity Rate
series.tooltip: Yield on 2-year US Treasury debt. Reflects market expectations for the policy rate over the near term.

series.label: 10-Year Treasury Constant Maturity Rate
series.tooltip: Yield on 10-year US Treasury debt. A common benchmark for long-dated project and infrastructure finance.

series.label: 10-Year Treasury Minus 2-Year Treasury Spread
series.tooltip: The 10-year yield minus the 2-year yield. A sustained negative value (an inverted curve) has historically preceded recessions, though it is a signal and not a forecast.

series.label: 30-Year Fixed Rate Mortgage Average
series.tooltip: Average 30-year fixed mortgage rate. Included as a proxy for household borrowing costs, which influence local housing supply and workforce mobility near new facilities.

series.label: Chicago Fed National Financial Conditions Index
series.tooltip: A composite index of US financial conditions. Positive values indicate conditions tighter than average, negative values looser than average. Zero is the historical average, not a neutral target.

series.label: Commercial and Industrial Loans, All Commercial Banks
series.tooltip: Outstanding commercial and industrial bank loans. Growth indicates banks are extending credit to businesses, one channel through which capital-intensive projects get funded.

series.label: Commercial Real Estate Loans, All Commercial Banks
series.tooltip: Outstanding commercial real estate loans at commercial banks. Data centers are financed partly through CRE channels, so growth here reflects credit availability for that asset class.

series.label: Consumer Price Index for All Urban Consumers
series.tooltip: The most widely cited US consumer price index. The KPI shows the year-over-year percent change, which is what is normally meant by 'the inflation rate'.

series.label: Personal Consumption Expenditures Price Index
series.tooltip: The Federal Reserve's preferred inflation measure. Tends to run slightly below CPI because of differences in weighting and scope.

series.label: Real Gross Domestic Product
series.tooltip: Inflation-adjusted US economic output, reported quarterly. The KPI shows year-over-year growth.

series.label: Industrial Production Total Index
series.tooltip: Real output of manufacturing, mining, and utilities. Utility output is relevant context for electricity-intensive facilities.

series.label: Unemployment Rate
series.tooltip: National unemployment rate, published monthly by the Bureau of Labor Statistics. This is separate from — and more current than — the county unemployment estimates on this platform, which come from the Census ACS 5-year survey.

series.label: All Employees, Total Nonfarm
series.tooltip: Total nonfarm payroll employment. The headline monthly US jobs number.

series.label: Initial Claims
series.tooltip: Weekly new filings for unemployment insurance. The most timely widely-available labor market indicator.

series.label: Advance Retail Sales, Retail and Food Services
series.tooltip: Monthly retail and food service sales — a proxy for household demand.

series.label: New Privately-Owned Housing Units Started
series.tooltip: Annualised rate of new private housing construction starts. Indicates regional construction capacity and labor competition for building trades.

series.label: New Privately-Owned Housing Units Authorized by Building Permits
series.tooltip: Permits authorised for new private housing. Leads housing starts, so it is a forward-looking construction signal.
